verdict.rationale: Mastra Code is a terminal agent you install and run yourself. It is installed through a package manager, keeps its storage in local SQLite by default (or a remote database you choose), and can be embedded in your own CI scripts and servers, so the core runs on user-controlled infrastructure. The docs never frame this as self-hosting, and inference relies on third-party provider accounts. Missing for 10: explicit self-hosting or deployment documentation, an open-source license or source-availability evidence, support for local or self-hosted models, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Run `mastracode update` to install the latest version with the package manager that installed Mastra Code.
Connect to a remote database instead of the default local SQLite:
`runMC` never calls `process.exit` and never writes to global streams, so it is safe to embed in CI scripts and servers.
Use it to embed Mastra Code in custom applications or extend its functionality.
